authorized_future_implementation_surface.note: Authorized for the SUCCESSOR mission only. None of these paths is created, modified or touched by this mission. Naming follows existing repository convention (scripts/ods-*.ts with a matching tests/ods/ods-*.test.ts), verified against the directory listings at BASE_SHA this session.

paths.role: The single Controller v0 script. At most 400 lines. Thin deterministic node selector/router that invokes the existing gates listed in ODS_CONTROLLER_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json controller_v0_design.reuse_not_duplicate.surfaces and classifies their output into the frozen state model and stop taxonomy.
paths.hosts_controller_policy: Yes. ODS_CONTROLLER_POLICY — including its required immutableByConvention[] array — is an exported const in this script, mirroring the existing precedent of DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS and PROTECTED_GRANTS in scripts/ods-scope.ts. Hosting the policy here rather than in a new data file is deliberate: it satisfies the zero-second-state-store ceiling and keeps the policy testable by the same closed-world enumeration pattern already used for PROTECTED_GRANTS in tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts.

paths.role: Tests for Controller v0, including the mandatory non-vacuity negative controls E3 through E7 in ODS_CONTROLLER_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json exit_criteria_for_controller_v0_implementation, and the closed-world enumeration assertions for immutableByConvention[] and the stop-class list.
paths.ceiling_note: The 400-line ceiling constrains the controller script only. Tests are not capped, because capping test volume would create a direct incentive to under-test the guard.

authorized_future_implementation_surface.closed_world: This list is exhaustive. A path not enumerated here is NOT authorized for the successor mission, and its appearance in a diff is an UNEXPECTED_CHANGED_PATH STOP — never a retroactive scope inference from the fact that it changed.

mutation.M1: DEFERRED_TO_SUCCESSOR_MISSION. Meaningful mutation controls for this authority test its guards — immutableByConvention enforcement, the single-rerun flake ceiling, the DB-execution refusal, and the fableEligible self-grant prohibition — none of which exist as executable code until Controller v0 is implemented. They are frozen as exit criteria E3 through E6 in ODS_CONTROLLER_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json and are mandatory for the successor mission. Asserting a mutation control here would be vacuous, and vacuous controls are precisely what the ODS negative-control doctrine forbids.
